_meta.description: Legal input domain + provenance for every pricing assumption key. The admin DB seed bounds, the admin editor UI, and the per-job panel all derive from this file. kind=enum has a closed 'values' list; kind=range has [min,max,step]; kind=flag is a two-choice {0,1}; kind=scalar_published is a provider-published single value with a source_url, edited within bounds but flagged if it drifts.

dax_node_gib.derived_from: EC2 R-family node RAM (dax.r*.large=16 ... 16xlarge=512 GiB; smallest t-class ≈ 2 GiB). AWS-side quantity; GCP only constrains the output (Memorystore M5 tier ≈ 300 GiB max single-tier representation).
dax_node_gib.source: AWS DAX node types run on EC2 R-family memory nodes (large=16, doubling to 16xlarge=512 GiB); GCP ceiling: Memorystore for Redis tiers M1-M5 (4/10/35/100/300 GiB)

dynamodb_rcu_to_reads_sec.source: workload-dependent utilization knob. 0 = passthrough at AWS cost (default, ratio 1, matches data/pricing_matrix.json). >0 maps RCU-hours to Cloud Firestore Read Ops as rcu*3600 reads/hr; at 1.0 this over-projects ~8.3x (AWS $0.00013/RCU-hr vs 3600 reads x $3e-7 Firestore = $0.00108). Ratio-1 utilization point is ~0.12 if an op-native projection is wanted instead of passthrough.

dynamodb_wcu_to_writes_sec.source: workload-dependent utilization knob. 0 = passthrough at AWS cost (default, ratio 1, matches data/pricing_matrix.json). >0 maps WCU-hours to Cloud Firestore Entity Writes as wcu*3600 writes/hr; at 1.0 this over-projects ~5.0x (AWS $0.00065/WCU-hr vs 3600 writes x $9e-7 Firestore = $0.00324). Ratio-1 utilization point is ~0.20 if an op-native projection is wanted instead of passthrough.

inferentia_chip_to_tpu.source: 0 = passthrough at AWS cost (default, ratio 1). No public Inferentia-vs-TPU benchmark exists, so projecting a TPU price would assert an unverified performance/price equivalence; passthrough carries the AWS cost with a Cloud TPU label and avoids that. Set >0 to map to Cloud TPU v5e at a declared PRICE ratio (e.g. 0.19 matches inf1.xlarge $0.228/hr vs TPU v5e $1.20/chip-hr) once a defensible equivalence exists.

lambda_mb_per_vcpu.derived_from: Cloud Run CPU:memory envelope caps memory at 4096 MiB per vCPU; AWS Lambda allocates 1 vCPU per 1769 MB as the as-is reference
lambda_mb_per_vcpu.source: GCP ceiling: Cloud Run max 4 GiB per vCPU (https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/services/cpu); AWS reference 1 vCPU/1769 MB (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-function-common.html)

looker_studio_pro_seat_usd.source: Data Studio Pro (Google reverted the name Looker Studio -> Data Studio on 2026-04-11; the paid tier is now 'Data Studio Pro'). Per-user, per-project license: $9/user/project/month. VERIFIED 2026-11-09: Google no longer lists a price publicly (old page cloud.google.com/looker-studio/pricing 404s; official number is only in the Cloud console checkout). $9 is CORROBORATED by multiple independent third-party sources (trustradius.com, coupler.io, databloo.com, whatagraph.com) and the 2026 rebrand coverage (ppc.land, dataslayer.ai). Gold-standard confirmation is the Cloud console; keep flagged until an admin confirms there.

memorydb_node_gib.derived_from: EC2 R-family node RAM (db.r6g/r7g.large=16 ... 16xlarge=512 GiB; db.t4g.small ≈ 2 GiB). AWS-side quantity; GCP only constrains the output (Memorystore M5 tier ≈ 300 GiB max single-tier representation).
memorydb_node_gib.source: AWS MemoryDB node types db.r6g/r7g.* run on EC2 R-family memory nodes (large=16, doubling to 16xlarge=512 GiB); GCP ceiling: Memorystore for Redis tiers M1-M5 (4/10/35/100/300 GiB)
